decisions: umbrella Amendment M, Ruling 1 and Ruling 3
umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 1 and Ruling 2
what_lands: The third of the fourteen. cast_proc/receipt_walk retires in Amendment L, Ruling 1's whole shape: the family's eight mechanics declare both halves (eight ViewTag.THEORETICAL pair previews and eight APPLIED walk halves delivered as HolderPacket, PER_HOLDER, PAIRED), damage._add_item_proc_damage stamps pair_preview_of on every row it authors and hands the walk an AuthoredDeclaration per event under it, interpreters.cast_proc.WALK_INTERPRETER registers at (CAST_PROC, RECEIPT_WALK), and survival.transitions.apply_declared_price prices the declaration at the resistance that packet met. The deferral row leaves docs/behavior-frontier.json in the same commit with the reason its surviving compiled-lane twin can no longer share corrected there (R-36).
why_this_family_is_startable_now: It was blocked by the same term that stopped active_cast, and named as blocked in that receipt: 'cast_proc is blocked by the same term on the same stage and is not attempted -- eclipse.proc and scouts_slingshot.proc are physical packets the same window rescales, its covering scenarios hold no such window either.' Both halves of that are now answered. Umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 1's per-packet resistance term landed at 319f076, Ruling 2's source-derived census is green and is the precondition on any further retirement (78df1f8), and Ruling 3's window-armed covering scenarios landed at 45652c5/eb68690 -- one of which, lethality_window_assassin_roster, is now a covering scenario of this family, so the window this family's physical packets meet is inside the enumerated population rather than outside every baseline.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 -- no baseline moves inside any semantic commit of this slice. The code lands against the committed baselines plus this allowlist; a re-capture, if the measurement ever asks for one, is the integration agent's own commit.

qualifying_population.rule: R-20's second half. The count is not readable off the pre-change tree by inspection: this slice moves where a number comes from rather than editing a formula, so which leaves can move is a property of which participants hold a declaring owner of the family, and that is a fact about the committed scenario set rather than about the diff. The population is therefore enumerated from committed artifacts -- the committed docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json at c9c2398, whose own fields are derived from the behaviour catalog and from scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json's scenario subtrees -- before the slice's first src/ edit. Any occurrence outside it is an unexpected one and stops the slice exactly as an over-count would.
qualifying_population.predicate: Every committed coupled scenario that puts a declaring owner of the cast_proc family on a participant. The eight owners are read live from the behaviour catalog over rule_owners() -- Eclipse, Hextech Alternator, Luden's Echo, Malignance, Scout's Slingshot, Stormsurge, Zaz'Zak's Realmspike, Zeke's Convergence -- which is the same family-to-owner join golden_snapshot.receipt_walk_families() makes for the coverage guard, so the population and the guard cannot disagree about which rosters can see the family.
qualifying_population.method: scripts.receipt_walk_schedule.population_size over each selected scenario subtree of the committed coupled baseline -- the same instrument, and the same conservative bound, the retirement schedule uses for the remaining rows: the whole scenario subtree, because a slice that moves a family's pricing can move any aggregate downstream of it inside that scenario.
qualifying_population.why_this_population_can_see_the_two_term: Two of the eleven are the reason the count is worth having rather than a number. amp_armed_mage_roster arms the holder's magic amp and its ability part amp on an Ahri holding Stormsurge, so the declared amp term Amendment M, Ruling 1 ruled is exercised on a proc rather than read at 1.0. lethality_window_assassin_roster arms a Voltaic Cyclosword Firmament window, which is the window that stopped active_cast's first attempt, so a physical proc re-priced inside it is inside this population rather than invisible to every baseline. Three of the eleven are score-mode scenarios, which is the other ledger shape (the tuple ledger), so the composition path the optimizer takes is covered too.

pair_engine_population.why: scripts/golden_baseline.json is the one-attacker pair-engine surface, and this slice adds no pair-engine arithmetic: the two stamps it adds pair-side -- pair_preview_of on each proc row and the row's own declaration on the events under it -- are not leaves that baseline holds, which records each build's sorted breakdown_keys and its total_damage and neither a row's inner fields nor an event. Zero pair-engine golden diffs is therefore a declared population of zero rather than an observation, and a single diff there stops the slice.

qualifying_population.predicted: 0 occurrences inside a population of 5706. The walk's from-declaration price and the pair engine's are the same real number with the multiplications associated differently -- the pair engine mitigates and then applies the holder's amps, the walk composes the amps pre-mitigation and mitigates once (Amendment M, Ruling 1) -- so the two agree to within one unit in the last place, four orders of magnitude below the 0.005 golden equality grades to (R-13). The resistance each side prices at is the same one under Amendment N, Ruling 1. A leaf that did move could only move by 0.01, which qualifies under none of R-15's three tests.

what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.why_it_is_written_down_in_advance: This family's pair pricing is not one multiplication. A declaration that reproduced the active's shape would silently drop three per-packet factors the pair engine applies, which is Amendment M, Ruling 1's second forbidden shape -- a deletion wearing a re-spelling's name -- so what each declaration owes is enumerated here before the edit rather than discovered by whichever total came out short.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_per_packet_magnitude: raw_per_proc for a cooldown proc, times the charged-bounce target share damage._charged_proc_target_share resolves for this roster slot, because that share is a pair-local allocation of one application and not an amplifier. Zaz'Zak's Realmspike is the one owner it is ever anything but 1.0 for. The ultimate procs fold their own duration scaling in the same way: Malignance's raw is scaled by the effective Hatefog window before mitigation.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_attack_class: AttackClass.ABILITY where the pair engine applied the holder's ability amp to that packet and AttackClass.OTHER where it did not, decided per event rather than per rule. The engine gates the amp per trigger against the Actualizer window (damage.py's actualizer_active_until), so a proc that fired after the window closed earns no part amp, and a declaration that claimed ABILITY for every trigger would hand the walk an amp the pair engine had already declined to pay.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_resistance: Absent at authoring, which is the correct reading for a packet that met the fight's published figure, and restated by damage._restate_declaration at every site that re-prices the packet afterwards (Amendment N, Ruling 1). This is the term that makes a physical proc inside a Firmament window price to what the engine priced it at.

no_baseline_moves: R-32's five baselines are untouched by every commit of this slice. docs/behavior-frontier.json and docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json are machine-derived receipts whose counters this slice moves, so they move with it (R-36); holding them back would make the slice red against a gate it is forbidden to contain.

measured_after.golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. The declared pair-engine population of 0 held: the two stamps this slice adds pair-side are a row field and an event field, and that baseline records neither.
measured_after.coupled_golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. Zero of the 5706 enumerated leaves moved, which is the predicted reading: the walk's from-declaration price and the pair engine's are the same real number associated differently, priced at the same resistance under Amendment N, Ruling 1.

what_the_walk_actually_priced.why_it_is_recorded: A zero on a baseline is evidence the family's numbers did not move; it is not evidence the walk priced anything. This is the second half, read off survival.transitions.apply_declared_price itself rather than reconstructed.
what_the_walk_actually_priced.measured: Across the family's covering coupled scenarios the walk priced two declarations from this family -- eclipse.proc and stormsurge.proc -- one pricing per (source_key, rule), each equal to the declaration's own price re-computed from the resistances that packet met, and each strictly between zero and the amped raw magnitude.
what_the_walk_actually_priced.eclipse_is_the_receipt_only_member: eclipse.proc is the one rule of the eight the compiled kernel refuses (ReceiptOnly, SURVIVAL_LEDGER_TRANSITION scope, its self-shield payload). Its receipt-walk half is exactly what a receipt-only rule was always supposed to have, and it is also the family's one coarse-row path -- a late-phase proc whose ledger holds no certifiable attack boundary authors no damage_events, so the row-level declaration and _row_declaration_share are what keep the walk from finding a packet stamped as re-priced with nothing to re-price it from.

the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound.why_it_is_recorded: R-01 row 8 reads the optimizer's own search over the bench builds, which no enumerated coupled population contains, and it is the gate that stopped this family's predecessor.
the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound.measured: bench_coupled_optimizer.py --fixed-work --isolate --json: cassiopeia_3champ 4003.1 / residual 79, cassiopeia_5champ 5010.8 / 19, mundo_3champ 3305.0 / 12, syndra_mandate_3champ 4642.3 / 98 -- every winner and score identical to what campaign-fingerprints.json pins, and identical again with --no-compiled (routing_divergences empty on all four). Three of the four bench winners hold Stormsurge or Malignance, so this family's declarations are priced inside the searched builds and not only inside the coupled scenarios.

measured_after.oracle_receipts_owed: None. R-19 owes an investigator per qualifying occurrence (R-15) and there were none, in a population enumerated in advance and non-empty -- 5706 leaves across eleven rosters, two of which arm the terms the pricing stage carries and three of which are the score-mode ledger shape.
